claims.text: At stage-2 keycloak/donhang-realm.json (realm `donhang`) defines six users: five with realmRoles ["customer"], lan.do@example.com with ["staff"]; each entry fixes its own id and has username, email, emailVerified, firstName, lastName and a password credential.
Trần Minh Anh's Keycloak entry: id 92f6ba26-729c-4d61-854b-c04c9f2db11a, username/email anh.tran@example.com, firstName "Minh Anh", lastName "Trần", realmRoles ["customer"].

At stage-2 db/seed.sql inserts five customers (ids 1-5), Trần Minh Anh as (1, 'Trần Minh Anh', 'anh.tran@example.com', 'Hà Nội'); no row for lan.do@example.com. docker-compose mounts it into the db container's initdb, so a fresh lab database has 5 rows in customers.
At stage-2 Customer has Id, FullName, Email, City and a nullable IdentitySubject (Keycloak's id, the token's `sub`); no username, password or role.

Migration AddCustomerIdentitySubject adds customers.identity_subject (unique index), then runs one UPDATE per email setting it to the five customer users' Keycloak ids; it fills only rows already present.
The API reads `sub` from the validated token and looks the customer up with ICustomerRepository.FindByIdentitySubjectAsync.

A valid token for lan.do@example.com (no customers row) on GET /api/v1/orders gets 403, not an empty list: CurrentCustomerAsync finds no customer by identity_subject, returns null, and the action returns Forbid().

claims.text: Definition: a bounded context is a boundary inside which one model and its language apply; outside it the same word may mean something else; it is a boundary of a model, not necessarily of a deployment.
claims.source_hint: DDD literature (strategic design: bounded context); glossary.yaml bounded-context short_en

claims.text: When two models describe the same people for different purposes, link them by one id and let each keep its own fields rather than share one class, because a shared class couples sign-in changes to ordering code; cost: duplicated data such as email.

One meaning per word is required inside a bounded context, not across a company; a company-wide meaning often ends up too broad or takes a long negotiation. Opposing view: for a report spanning the whole business a team may agree one definition for that report.

git grep -n prints matching lines with file and line number; -F matches literally; a tag as <tree> searches files at that tag; paths after -- limit the search. For lan.do: 2 realm lines (username, email), none in seed.sql; for anh.tran: 2 realm lines, 1 seed.sql line.
